passage: At the edge of the wheat fields behind the village school, Hemant and Tushar stood nose to nose. "I'm captain!" "No, I am!" The other boys sat on the grass, waiting with the ball. Hemant was about to storm off when Tushar said, "If I'm captain today, you're captain tomorrow. Then we swap." Hemant thought. It sounded fair. "Me first tomorrow?" "Fine," said Tushar. They shook hands, picked teams, and the game began. On the next day Hemant chose the sides, and Tushar lined up behind him without a word. The fight did not come back that week.

qa.q: How did Hemant and Tushar decide who is captain?
qa.a: Whoever is captain today, the other is captain tomorrow, and then they swap.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling just before Tushar suggested a swap?
qa.a: Hemant was angry and about to storm off, showing how much being captain mattered.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the boys use, and why?
qa.a: They could toss a coin or ask the other boys to vote, since both give a fair answer quickly. Sharing the job with two captains is another option.

qa.q: How do the boys waiting on the grass see the argument?
qa.a: The other boys sit and wait with the ball, so they probably feel bored and impatient, and want the fight settled so the game can start.

grounding: The fight is about who is captain, and the boys agree to alternate the job each day so both are treated fairly.

subtype: Approach: offering a fair fix like taking turns [Action]
passage: Every lunch break in the schoolyard in Valencia, the football game started with the same fight: Pablo wanted to be captain, and so did Diego. On Monday they shoved each other and the whole break was lost to arguing. On Tuesday Mei, who kept the ball, said, "Can't you just take turns?" The two boys looked at each other. "Me today, you tomorrow," Diego offered. "And then swap every day after that," said Pablo. They shook on it. Mei wrote the days on a card and stuck it on the ball bag. On Wednesday, when Diego started to argue out of habit, Pablo just pointed at the card: WED, PABLO. Diego laughed, dropped his water bottle by the wall, and joined Pablo's team.

qa.q: How did Diego seem to feel when Pablo pointed at the card?
qa.a: He laughed, so he seemed at ease with it, knowing his own turn was fair and coming.

qa.q: What could the boys do if more players want to be captain?
qa.a: Add them to Mei's card in turn; writing the days down is what stopped the same quarrel starting again.

qa.q: How did the lunch-break fights look to Mei?
qa.a: Mei watched a whole break lost to arguing, so Mei was probably fed up, and glad the card fixed it.

grounding: Shows two boys ending a fight over who is captain by agreeing to swap captains each day, which is fair and stops the quarrel recurring.

subtype: Approach: offering a fair fix like taking turns [Action]
passage: At the Sunday cricket camp in the Ludhiana stadium, Gurpreet and Amandeep had spent twenty minutes arguing over who would captain the practice match. Coach Baljit blew his whistle. "No match until you two sort it out." They glared at each other by the boundary rope. Then Amandeep said, "Okay. What if you're captain today, I'm captain next Sunday, and we keep swapping?" Gurpreet thought. "And whoever isn't captain opens the batting." "Deal." They wrote it in the back of the coach's register: G, A, G, A. The match started ten minutes later. The next Sunday, nobody argued at all.

qa.q: Where did they write the plan?
qa.a: In the back of the coach's register: G, A, G, A.

qa.q: What might Gurpreet have felt when Amandeep suggested swapping?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and fairly treated, and added his own idea about opening the batting.

qa.q: Why is swapping a better fix than one boy giving in?
qa.a: It treats both fairly every week, so neither feels he lost, and the same quarrel doesn't come back next Sunday.

qa.q: How does Coach Baljit see the problem?
qa.a: Coach Baljit sees twenty minutes lost to arguing and insists they sort it out themselves before any match.

grounding: Illustrates two boys settling a quarrel over captaincy by agreeing to alternate captains, a fair fix that stops the fight from returning.
